title: Loops — practice quiz
description: A short check on `for` loops, `while` loops, and `break` / `continue`. This quiz does not run GDScript; it only checks that the ideas landed.

questions.explain: `range(3)` starts at `0` and stops before `3`, so you get `0`, `1`, and `2`. It does not include `3`.

questions.prompt: What does `break` do in a loop?
choices: Skips one item and keeps looping
Restarts the loop from the beginning
questions.explain: `break` leaves the loop early. Once the monster finds a target, there is no need to keep scanning.

questions.prompt: What does `continue` do in a loop?
choices: Skips the rest of this pass and goes to the next item
questions.explain: `continue` skips the rest of the current pass only. The loop keeps going with the next item, unlike `break`, which stops the loop entirely.

choices: As soon as its condition is no longer true
questions.explain: A `while` loop keeps going as long as its condition is true, and it stops as soon as that condition becomes false. If the condition never becomes false, the loop can run forever.
